MAP milestones (proposed)

- Metrics logged: P50/P95 latency (ms), tokens/sec, requests/sec, TTFT, GPU utilization, memory headroom, KV cache hit rate

Vanessa / team —

Quick runbook notes to include in the MAP:
- Test harness: fixed seed sampling + deterministic eval path for latency; we’ll run 1000 warm-up requests then record 10k steady-state samples
- Prompt distribution: 64/256/512/1024 token buckets (sample ratios to be confirmed with Acme)
- Batching: evaluate latencies at no-batching and at configured micro-batch sizes (2, 4, 8) to model PLG vs batched throughput workloads
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for conversational threads; measure hit-rate impact on TTFT and P95
- MIG notes: expect ~20-30% higher P95 for MIG slices compared to full GPU for small prompts due to reduced kernel parallelism; throughput per-dollar improves with higher slice density in batch workloads
- Concurrency heuristic: start sweep at 1 -> 200 concurrent sessions; measure at steady state (after warm-up)

Preliminary hardware expectation (ballpark)
- H100 (full): best P50/P95 for low-latency single-request workloads; highest raw throughput for long sequences
- A100 (full): solid latency, slightly higher P95 vs H100 on our kernels for 512+ tokens
- L40S: cost-effective for throughput-focused batch workloads — slightly higher latency at low concurrency
- MIG: useful for high-density multi-tenant trials but plan for ~10-20% extra margin in SLA

I’ve dropped the perf scripts and internal template folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PerfRunbooks

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the questions. We updated the MAP and experiment results summary and attached the final artifacts: redwood_map_benchmark_results_v2.pdf and hw_fit_matrix_a100_h100_l40s.csv (see attachments). Quick answers and running-summary: 

TTFT definitions we captured:
- Cold-start TTFT: includes model load + first token (measured from request arrival to first token emitted when model is not warm in RAM)
- Warm TTFT: first-token latency once model and KV cache are resident (this is what we use for steady-state SLOs)

Pricing / canary / recommended HW fit (high level):
- Results (baseline runs, median across representative 512-token prompt set):
  - H100 (full 80GB): P50=22ms, P95=38ms, Warm TTFT=28ms, throughput=4200 tokens/sec, sustainable concurrency target=120 requests (chat RTP)
  - A100 (full 80GB): P50=34ms, P95=55ms, Warm TTFT=40ms, throughput=3200 tokens/sec, sustainable concurrency target=90 requests
  - L40S: P50=48ms, P95=65ms, Warm TTFT=55ms, throughput=2800 tokens/sec, sustainable concurrency target=70 requests
  - A100 4x MIG (20GB slices): per-slice P95 ~70-85ms at comparable per-slice memory bound workloads; higher density but ~25% lower single-req throughput
  - H100 2x MIG: per-slice P95 ~55-68ms; better density than A100 MIG but still worse than full GPU for low-latency workloads

Recommendation: For Acme's latency-sensitive product path, we recommend H100 full machines for the canary and initial production. L40S is a cost-effective option for non-critical batch scoring jobs. If cost-per-inference density is the priority, plan a staged MIG trial with conservative SLO margins and automated fallback to full GPU variants when P95 > threshold.

Canary plan (included in attached MAP):
- Canary cohort: 5% traffic for 48 hours
- Success criteria: P95 <= agreed threshold and error rate < 0.1%
- Rollback triggers: sustained P95 breach for 15 consecutive minutes or error spike > 0.1%

Next steps
- Procurement: Laura will send a 6-month pilot pricing sheet (line items for H100/A100/L40S and MIG overlay) by EOD 2027-05-11
- Engineering: Ben will request dataset access and scope the full runbook; we'll schedule baseline runs the week of 2027-05-17 if sign-off occurs by 2027-05-12
- Sign-off: Jordan/procurement to confirm by 2027-05-12 to meet the above cadence

Attachments referenced: redwood_map_benchmark_results_v2.pdf (summary + raw metrics), hw_fit_matrix_a100_h100_l40s.csv (detailed per-run CSV), map_milestones_20270510.xlsx (final MAP schedule)
